audit_rule: NOTHING counts as done until an adversarial round comes back clean AT THE GATE BELOW. Rewritten 2026-09-07 (AUDIT-RULE-V2) after Phase A ran SIX rounds without converging and Phase D took THIRTEEN. The intent is unchanged -- do not ship uncontrolled -- but the previous version could not terminate. Three defects, three fixes. || (1) THE GATE IS THE ONLY THING THAT COUNTS, AND THE REVIEWER IS TOLD SO. A finding blocks only if it can put a WRONG NUMBER in front of a user or on a broker order, or CORRUPT PERSISTED DATA. Everything else -- wording, comments, test hygiene, dead code, stale records, latent defects with no reachable path -- is not a finding for this purpose, and the audit brief must instruct the reviewer NOT TO REPORT IT AT ALL. Round 6 returned 16 findings of which 5 were real bugs; the other 11 cost triage time and are now recorded forever. An adversarial reviewer with no severity floor ALWAYS finds something, so 'clean' was unreachable by construction. || (2) THE TARGET SHRINKS, IT DOES NOT GROW. Round 1 reviews the whole change. Round N>1 reviews ONLY what changed since round N-1 -- the previous round's fixes -- plus any interaction those fixes have with already-reviewed code. Re-auditing the cumulative diff every round is what turned each round's fixes into the next round's findings: 9 of round 5's 15 findings sat in round 3-4 FIX CODE, including BOTH BLOCKING, while the original Phase A implementation produced ZERO BLOCKING across rounds 4 and 5. The feature was converging; the fixing was not. || (3) THE EXIT IS OBJECTIVE, NOT THE REVIEWER'S SILENCE. audit_clean is true when a round returns ZERO gate-level findings. Such a round triggers no fixes, so there is nothing new for a further round to look at -- and the round that reviewed the last batch of fixes was already the second look. One zero-finding round ends it. || HARD CAP: if a phase reaches THREE rounds without going clean, STOP AUDITING AND TELL KENNETH. That is evidence the batch is too big to audit, not that it needs a fourth round. || BATCH SIZE is the root cause the gate merely exposes. Phase A was 62 files across every layer of the app; nothing that size audits to clean. Split work so one change touches one layer, or roughly 500 lines. A change that size clears in one round. || FIXING: only gate-level findings are fixed in-branch. Nothing else -- not 'while I am here', not a one-line nit. Everything else is logged against main. Rounds 4 and 5 fixed 10 and 12 findings against a rule that already said this, and that non-compliance is a large part of why the loop stayed alive. || audit_rounds counts rounds RUN. A phase with status=shipped and audit_clean=false is NOT finished. This applies to `already_shipped` entries identically -- being written in that list means the CODE is done, never that the WORK is.

(2) contract_validator.py had never been converted -- the worked example (75% IV hard-rejected at max_iv_rank: 70) lives there at line 98, not in stock_scorer. (3) /api/config/iv-thresholds served one unqualified `pass_max` the client applied to whatever figure it held; it now serves abs_*/rank_* and no bare name. ROUND 1'S FOUR BLOCKING -- (a), (b) and (c) are now FIXED IN-BRANCH per the severity gate; (d) remains OPEN and blocks the round, because it needs Kenneth's call rather than an implementation. (b) portfolioStore.ts version 4, same omission; positions the reconcile keeps as pending/offline are never overwritten, so for those it is permanent. (c) Step 3's 'IV rank pass max' execution parameter is INERT on the default path: stock_scorer.py:1036 writes cfg['vol']['iv_rank_pass_max'] while _rule_vol:896 reads iv_abs_pass_max whenever basis != 'rank'. Verified by running it -- user sets 20, absolute IV 30 returns PASS; written to the key _rule_vol actually reads it returns CAUTION. The identical rename WAS done in contract_validator's override table in this same commit and forgotten here. (d) spread_builder.choose_primary decides bear_call (credit, short premium) vs bear_put (debit) from a basis-blind resolved figure against one unqualified threshold (settingsStore ivRankThreshold: 50), with iv_basis computed two lines away at scan.py:612 and not passed -- so 60% absolute IV and the 60th percentile pick opposite structures on a broker order, and `iv_rank or 0.0` maps 'no IV at all' to 0, always bear_put. TWO CLAIMS IN COMMIT 71e317e5 ARE FALSE, corrected here: 'no verdict changes today' -- a strike with no vendor IV used to reach _score_iv_rank as 0.0 (augment's old `round(float(c.get('ivRank', 0)), 1)`) scoring a spurious iv_score 100, and now arrives None scoring a neutral 50; measured, one contract moved CAUTION(47) -> REJECT(40). And 'the resolution is defined ONCE per side' -- true on the frontend, false on the backend, where augment.py:78-89 and scan.py:609-618 are two implementations that already differ in detail (augment rounds to 1dp, scan does not; only scan has the Black-Scholes third branch). FIX ROUND 1 (this commit): (a)/(b) both stores now DROP a pre-split ivRank/ivPercentile rather than guess its basis -- scanStore v12->v13 via stripLegacyIvFromScanResult, portfolioStore v4->v5 via stripLegacyIvFields, both VERSION-GATED because the strip is the one non-idempotent branch in either migrate() and would otherwise discard the genuine rank a post-split row carries, on every load. The basis is not recoverable from the stored record: the two quantities share the 0-100 scale, and the only would-be discriminator (a pre-split ivPercentile of 0) exists on contractDetails but not on alternatives entries or portfolio rows, so it would take three rules for one quantity. And once the spot rallied past the stale mid's intrinsic, `_compute_iv_bs` refused and an ORDINARY ITM contract rendered 'Not computed'. FIX: `estimateFirstPassage` sends the `premium` it already resolved; `checkStructure` now fetches the contract quote alongside the stock quote it was already fetching (it was the only one of the three handlers not doing so) and falls back to `cd.mid`. The existing test could not catch this: the default `getContractQuote` mock returns 2.5, the same number as `contractDetails.mid`, so the assertion could not discriminate -- and its comment stated the stale mid as the INTENT ('this button fetches no contract quote'), the same defect-as-its-own-justification pattern round 1 of batch 1 found in risk.test.ts. Mock and comment both corrected. (2) A CUSTOM HOLD RANGE WAS GRADED AT SWING'S LINE. B2 deleted the client-side threshold resolution (`scoringHorizonFromLabel(context.horizon)`, which reads the display string Step 3 writes and is therefore ALREADY Custom-resolved) and replaced it by sending `context.horizonPreset` raw. `_PRESET_TO_HORIZON` maps a bare `custom` to `swing` because the request carries no hold range to resolve with. So a Custom 60-185d scan -- labelled 'Position (60-185d)' on this very card, graded on Position's parameter row in Step 3 -- had its stop cost graded against Swing's 0.70 instead of Position's 0.60, and the badge echoed `passMaxFraction 0.70` beside it: PASS at fraction 0.65 where the app's own horizon says CAUTION. The mirror case flips too (Custom holdMax <= 4 is Intraday/0.80 to the app, graded at Swing's 0.70). Live: RunScanButton writes `horizonPreset` verbatim and the repo's own fixtures carry {horizonPreset:'Custom', holdMax:185}. FIX: the two GATE call sites send `resolveParamsHorizon(preset, holdMax)`, which collapses Custom and passes every other key through UNCHANGED -- so Quarterly/SemiAnnual/Annual keep their own keys and the backend still maps all three to `position`, and the barrier race's own request (which keys its repricing table on the SEVEN-key preset, and must: repricing a 200-day hold like a 20-day one is the error that table exists to avoid) still sends the raw preset. An absent holdMax falls back to the preset row's own bound, not to 0, which `scoringHorizonForHold` would read as Intraday. Backend untouched: `horizon_preset` on these two endpoints feeds `compute_stop_cost` and nothing else (verified at contracts.py:545 and :965). FOUR MUTATIONS RUN, all four caught: each call site reverted to `cd.mid` (2 failures each), the raw preset key sent again (1), and the resolver collapsing every preset instead of only Custom (1). Four regression tests added plus a per-test `setContext(null)` -- the scan context is a module-level zustand store this file never reset, so the gate's horizon would otherwise depend on which tests ran before. Frontend 108 suites / 1282 tests, backend 2117 passed / 1 skipped, typecheck clean. ROUND 2 AGAINST THE FIXES HAS NOT RUN YET. ---- ROUND 2 AGAINST B2's FIXES (2026-09-08), target shrunk to commit 4ffdef62 alone per audit_rule's shrinking-target clause: CLEAN. ZERO gate-level findings. B2 IS CLEAN AFTER 2 ROUNDS (phase audit_rounds reads 4 -- two on batch 1, two on B2). Phase-level audit_clean stays FALSE because B3 is still outstanding and BLOCKED. The reviewer verified by EXECUTION: full frontend suite (108 suites / 1282 tests), tsc clean, backend test_stop_cost_gate 44 passed, state.py exit 0, and SEVEN mutations on the production file. Four were caught -- both call sites reverted to cd.mid, gateHorizon collapsing every preset, and checkStructure sending the raw preset. THREE WERE NOT: computeExitPlan's horizon_preset reverted to the raw preset, the estimate sub-fetch's likewise, and the `holdMax ?? presetByKey(...).holdMax` fallback changed to `?? 0`. All three are coverage asymmetry on code that is correct as written and none is a wrong number today (the holdMax fallback is unreachable: ScanContext.holdMax is a required number and every writer sets it), so per the severity gate they were logged rather than fixed -- over-fixing sub-floor items inside the audit target is the specific behaviour audit_rule v2 exists to stop. Also cleared: the new Promise.all leg composes correctly with checkStructure's abort/deadline/isFinished/isRealFailure machinery (the added leg is structurally identical to the one computeExitPlan and estimateFirstPassage have carried longer); `gateHorizon` is a string, so the missing useMemo costs nothing and the three callbacks are onClick handlers no effect depends on; the `cd` hoist reads the same closure-captured object at both points; and the new setContext(null) and mockClear are both LOAD-BEARING, not sanitisers masking a defect (deleting either breaks a test).  ---- B3 UNBLOCKED 2026-09-08 by B3-SCOPED-STOP-2026-09-08 (a RECONSTRUCTED decision -- read its provenance field before relying on it). The phase note's earlier 'B3 is BLOCKED, see open_questions' pointed at a question THAT WAS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN: no open_questions entry ever stated the blocker. What the blocker actually was, recovered by re-deriving it: the badge needs a scan-time stop and the scan produces none, plus an unresolved ownership conflict between the gate-basis spec (Phase B) and the later implementation plan (Phase C part 5). Both are settled by that decision. LESSON, and the second time this exact failure has cost a session: a status field that defers to another field must name the entry it defers to, or it is an assertion with no referent.  ---- B3 BUILT 2026-09-08, NOT YET AUDITED (status shipped_unaudited, audit_clean stays FALSE; audit_rounds stays 4 -- those are batch 1's two and B2's two, and B3 has had NONE). BACKEND: _process_symbol now prices the gate at scan time for the auto-picked contract -- `_atr` -> `compute_final_stop` (wider of structural or ATR floor) -> `compute_stop_cost` -- and TradeCardData carries `stopCostPct`/`stopCostStatus`. Guarded three ways: ATR<=0 refuses rather than grading a zero-distance stop, compute_stop_cost's own None covers an unsolvable IV or a sub-cent premium, and the whole block is wrapped so a gate that cannot price itself never takes the candidate down with it. It passes the contract's OWN absolute `iv`, never `iv_rank` -- that variable holds a PERCENTILE whenever iv_basis=='rank', and a mutation feeding it is caught by the tests. FRONTEND: cardToRow copies both onto WatchlistRow, `rankingStopCost` in lib/risk.ts turns the pair into a label/tooltip/status, and the step-4-ranking table renders a sortable STOP column -- as a StatusBadge when there is a verdict and as dim text when there is not, because a verdict-shaped badge with no verdict in it reads as a passing one. Not-computed sorts to the end so an ungraded candidate cannot float to the top of a cheapest-stop-first sort. NO scanStore version bump, deliberately: the pair is additive and optional, an old blob's absent value collapses to null in cardToRow and renders 'not computed -- re-run the scan' (spec test 9), and a no-op migration branch would mislead the next reader. Reasoning is written into scanStore's migrate. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not reading: six backend tests, five of which are mutation-tested (pricing at the flat invalidation, dropping the ATR guard, feeding the percentile as absolute IV, hardcoding PASS, and never attaching the gate -- ALL FIVE CAUGHT); 14 frontend tests. TWO REAL DEFECTS WERE FOUND IN MY OWN TESTS BEFORE THEY WERE TRUSTED, both of the kind that pass while proving nothing: (1) the first fixture was a hand-made flat candle feed that scores trend 0 and is REJECTed at the pre-screen, so every assertion iterated an empty list -- the module now asserts the candidate list is non-empty instead of skipping, and uses real OHLCV from tests/fixtures/; (2) the tests passed alone and FAILED IN THE FULL SUITE, twice over: /api/scan prefetches OHLCV from the DB (which test_scan_db_first seeds) and signal confidence is memoised in a SQLITE FILE ON DISK that survives between runs and feeds a scoring rule. Both are now pinned in the fixture. ONE DEFECT CAUGHT BY RE-READING MY OWN DIFF, not by a test: the scan passed the vendor `iv` straight into compute_stop_cost with no bound, while the structural-stop ENDPOINT bounds the same input to gt=1.0/le=500.0 to catch a decimal-convention slip (0.35 meaning 35%). Repriced at 0.35% vol, a contract reports almost its whole premium lost at any stop -- a confident, plausible, badly wrong CAUTION on every affected row, and a scan cannot 422 its way out of it. The scan now drops an out-of-band figure, logs it, and inverts the mid instead, which cannot disagree with the quote it came from. Two tests pin it (the suspect value must match the inverted-mid answer exactly, AND an in-band vendor IV must still change the answer -- otherwise the guard is a disguised iv=None), and removing the guard fails one of them. WHAT B3 DID NOT DO, per its decision: Phase C's piece 3 is untouched and `exit.invalidation` is not repointed. ---- B3 ROUNDS 1-2 (2026-09-08). ROUND 1: ONE gate-level finding, verified at file:line and reproduced numerically before fixing. The scan passed `contract["iv"]` into compute_stop_cost as iv_pct, commented as 'the contract's OWN absolute IV when the chain carried one'. FALSE whenever the ATM fill fired: on a chain with no vendor IV, the pre-existing block at scan.py:640 inverts the ATM mid and broadcasts that ONE number into every strike lacking an `iv`, so a 20-delta wing is handed the ATM's volatility. In-band, so the range guard could not catch it, and it flattens exactly the smile this gate exists to read. Supplying iv_pct also makes compute_stop_cost SKIP the mid inversion its own docstring calls the normal basis -- and that docstring names the hazard verbatim: 'a caller-supplied iv_pct need not reproduce the contract's own mid'. MEASURED (200/210C, 30 DTE, $4.41 mid, stop $192, Swing): the ATM's 25% prices 81% CAUTION where the contract's own mid gives 50% PASS -- 31 points and an INVERTED VERDICT, on the column the table sorts by. FIX (54ef1004): iv_pct=None unconditionally. The gate is `loss = premium - BS(stop,K,T,r,iv)`, which only subtracts like from like when the volatility reproduces the very mid `premium` came from; inversion guarantees that by construction, any supplied number can only break it. The out-of-band range guard went with it -- it sanitised an argument no longer passed, and a guard that could not catch the in-band case it was aimed at was never the protection it appeared to be. TESTS: two existing tests pinned the REMOVED behaviour, one asserting an in-band `iv` MUST change the answer -- the defect written down as a contract. Replaced by test_contract_iv_never_moves_the_gate, parametrised over 0.35 / 25.0 / 90.0 / 400.0, each CONFIRMED TO FAIL against the shipped code and pass after the fix, plus test_supplying_an_iv_would_have_changed_the_answer pinning the unit boundary so the four cannot pass vacuously. ROUND 2: CLEAN, zero gate-level findings, scoped to 54ef1004 alone per audit_rule v2. The reviewer verified by EXECUTION: confirmed the deletion is a pure removal (no control flow depended on it, opt_float still live at scan.py:963/1066/1108); traced that with iv_pct=None the sigma is inverted from the same `premium` that is the subtrahend base and the same spot used for ATM selection, so numerator and denominator are one vintage by construction; established _compute_iv_bs's only refusals return None (honest absence, not a wrong number) and that when it solves, BS(stop) < premium so `fraction` lands strictly inside (0,1) and no clamped 0% PASS is reachable; independently reproduced 81%/50% and swept stops 198->180 (15/34/50/67/76/87%, monotone, verdicts flipping at the 70% Swing line); and confirmed the only other compute_stop_cost callers (contracts.py:537/957) pass Pydantic-constrained gt=1.0,le=500.0 input, so removing the scan-local guard left nothing unsanitised. Backend 2128 passed, 1 skipped. PHASE B IS CLEAN AND MERGEABLE.

phases.name: Piece 3 -- scan-time finalStop
phases.note: SHIPPED AND MERGED to main at 430bdb24 (--no-ff), clean after 2 adversarial rounds. Both halves built (C1 backend, C2 frontend). WHAT C1 DID: the stock stop every trade card is built around is now the wider of the structural level and a 2xATR floor, resolved ONCE per symbol in `resolve_stock_stop` (scoring/exit_plan.py) and RECEIVED by `build_trade_plan` as a required `final_stop_price` keyword. `exit.invalidation` carries that number; a new `exit.finalStop` block (FinalStopOut: price, source, stopSource, structuralSource, structuralPrice, atrFloorPrice, distanceDollar, atr, computedAt) carries its provenance so the 'Bottom (final stop)' row can render before Compute Arithmetic Plan is ever pressed. B3's ranking badge no longer makes its own private `compute_final_stop` call -- it reads the same resolution, so the badge and the Invalidation field grade the same level by construction (pinned by test_scan_endpoint.py::test_scan_badge_and_invalidation_grade_the_same_stop). || DECISION FLAT-STOP-DEMOTED-2026-09-09, Kenneth's call: Step 3's 'Bullish stop %' / 'Bearish stop %' (rr_bullish/bearish_invalidation_pct) are DEMOTED TO A FALLBACK, not deleted. They are read only when ATR(14) is 0 -- a feed too short or too flat to form one true range, on which compute_final_stop would hand back a floor sitting exactly ON entry, i.e. a zero-width stop. On that path there is no structural level and no ATR floor to report, so NO finalStop block is sent and the ranking badge refuses to price: 'not computed', never a block of nulls that reads as 'we looked and found nothing'. Both halves pinned in test_scan_endpoint.py::test_scan_rr_bullish_invalidation_pct_override_bites_only_on_a_dead_feed -- inert on a real feed (so nobody 'fixes' it back into a live flat stop), live on a dead one (so a user-visible execution parameter has not gone silently dead). || /contracts/recompute-plan ECHOES the card's own finalStop rather than re-deriving one. `mergePlan` replaces `exit` wholesale, so an endpoint returning no stop would wipe finalStop and drop invalidation back to a flat percentage for exactly the cards a user hand-picked a contract on. A fresh candle fetch was the first draft and was WRONG twice over: it adds a network round trip to an interactive endpoint whose stated design is 'one contract's fields in the body, no chain', and a feed that has moved on since the scan would hand back a DIFFERENT stop -- the override silently moving the level, which is the failure part 3 exists to prevent. The stop is a STOCK level; which contract is traded has no bearing on where structure sits. || STILL OUTSTANDING (C2, frontend): plan section 5 parts 3-half, 4 and the card rendering. `finalStop` on the wire type; the 'Bottom (final stop)' row reading it before an Arithmetic Plan exists, with contract-priced sub-cells and recommendedSize at '--' (part 2); mergePlan/withCachedEstimate keeping the block across a Step 6 override; and the scanStore migration -- NOTE THE PLAN IS STALE HERE, it says 'v12 -> 13' and the store is at version 14, so the bump is 14 -> 15. || PART 5 (the ranking badge) IS ALREADY DONE and needs no work: B3 shipped exactly what it specifies -- two fields on WatchlistRow (stopCostPct/stopCostStatus), populated in cardToRow, one grid track in COLUMNS and TableRow. Verified 2026-09-09, do not rebuild it. || Backend on C1: 2150 passed, 1 skipped. RECONCILES rather than merely being green -- main stood at 2132, test_stock_stop_resolution.py adds 15 and test_scan_endpoint.py nets +3 (one flat-override test replaced by four), test_trade_plan.py nets 0 (four flat-percentage tests replaced by four received-stop ones). || C2 (frontend). `TradeCardData.exit.finalStop` carries the provenance and `exit.invalidation` became `number | null`. The 'Bottom (final stop)' row now renders FROM THE SCAN before Compute Arithmetic Plan is ever pressed -- price, both candidates and the gap between them, plus the justification prose -- with 'Contract value at stop' and 'Max loss if stopped' printed as '--' rather than omitted (part 2: an absent row reads as 'there is no such thing', a dash reads as 'not computed yet'), and the risk-derived size already returned null without a plan so it needed no change. || SCANSTORE v14 -> v15, NOT 12 -> 13: the plan file is STALE on that number, the store had moved to 14 under Phase A. The branch strips `exit.invalidation` from every persisted candidate that carries no `finalStop` -- the same v13/v14 shape, a stored value that became a wrong number under a new reading. NOT cosmetic: `buildPaperPosition` stores that field as `PortfolioPosition.stop`, the level STOP_REACHED fires against, so a user ordering from a restored candidate would arm a -3% stop believing it structural, up to 3x tighter than the level the app now claims a position's stop is. Deleted rather than guessed -- the resolved stop needs a bar feed the client does not have. The branch is IDEMPOTENT (it skips any candidate that already has a block), which v13's own history says matters: that branch was edited nine commits after shipping and had to be re-run under a new version. || null renders 'not computed -- re-run the scan' on the Invalidation field (EditableKV gained a `nullLabel`; a bare dash beside an editable dollar field reads as zero) and fails `checkInvalidation`, so `missing_invalidation` blocks the send -- a branch that was EFFECTIVELY UNREACHABLE before piece 3, since the scan always sent a number. Two knock-ons that were NOT in the plan and are defects if skipped: (1) `checkTradeRisk` gained an optional `resolvedInvalidation`, threaded from step 7's `invalidationFor` through a new `invalidationBySymbol` prop on SendToBrokerDialog -- reading `card.exit.invalidation` alone would refuse a restored card FOREVER, even after the user typed a stop, which is the one gesture that fixes it; (2) `estimateFirstPassage` bails when the resolved stop is null, because `estimate_stock_first_passage` gates the stop leg on `invalidation_price > 0` and would have answered a probability of invalidation of ZERO -- read on screen as 'this trade cannot be stopped out'. The Estimate BUTTON stays enabled deliberately: that branch is reached only after the structural sub-fetch, and a structural level is a perfectly good stop for a restored card. || DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN'S PART 3, deliberate: the defence-in-depth splice lives in `mergePlan`, not `withCachedEstimate`. `withCachedEstimate` splices CLIENT-CACHED results (structuralStop, firstPassage, exitPlan) and `finalStop` is server data on the card, so it has no cache to splice from; `mergePlan` is where the wholesale `exit` replacement actually happens and is the only place both step-7 paths (active card at page.tsx:571, basket via resolveBasketCards) go through. When a response carries no block the card's is kept ALONG WITH ITS `invalidation` -- keeping the block while letting a flat-fallback number through would print a structural provenance row above a stop it does not describe. When both carry one the PLAN wins, because the plan's `invalidation` was computed against the plan's block and a mismatched pair is worse than either half. || Frontend on C2: typecheck clean, 111 suites / 1367 tests. RECONCILES: main stood at 110 / 1349, and the new work adds exactly 18 -- 7 in the new scanStoreStopMigration.test.ts (the only new suite), 4 on the TradeCard row, 4 on mergePlan's stop guard, 3 on the risk gate. || ROUND 1 (2026-09-09): ONE finding, BLOCKING, FIXED. NOT CLEAN -- round 2 pending. SCAN_RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION was not bumped, so the SERVER-SIDE scan cache replayed a pre-piece-3 flat stop as the resolved one and the v15 localStorage migration could never see it. A completed scan is persisted to `scan_sessions.last_result_json`, reloaded by `restore_from_db` on every backend start, and served verbatim by /api/scan/last; StoreHydration writes it into localStorage whenever `scanResult` is empty (fresh profile, cleared site data, second browser) and zustand stamps it at the CURRENT store version, so migrate never runs on it. Reproduced through the real endpoint: exit.invalidation 179.45 (= 185.00 x 0.97) served with finalStop None -- the card then asserts a stop in the editable field while the 'Bottom (final stop)' row inches above reads 'not computed', `checkInvalidation` passes, and `PortfolioPosition.stop` is armed at the flat level for STOP_REACHED (Gmail + Telegram) to fire against. Against a real resolved stop on the same fixture (2xATR floor at 176.60) the armed stop is $2.85-$7.35 too tight. This is VERBATIM the failure mode the Phase A guard's own comment at scan.py:1250 documents, reached one release later through the adjacent door. || ROOT CAUSE, and the fix goes at it rather than at the symptom: all THREE consumers (restore_from_db, /api/tradecards, /api/watchlist) tested for the ABSENCE of a version (`is None` / `is not None`), which is equivalent to a comparison only while exactly ONE bump exists. Every one is now `(blob.schema_version or 0) < SCAN_RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, so the next bump is honoured everywhere for free. Constant bumped 1 -> 2 with a per-version changelog in the comment. test_scan_result_vintage.py is parametrized over STALE_VERSIONS rather than over None, and that list explicitly includes `SCAN_RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION - 1` -- derived purely from `range(1, VERSION)` it would collapse to `[None]` the moment a bump is reverted or forgotten, going green on exactly the defect it exists to catch. Six of its tests fail against the pre-fix app code and pass against the fix (verified by stashing backend/app/ and re-running). /api/watchlist also gained its own vintage tests, which it had none of despite Phase A round 5 having caught it serving scores out of a blob the other two endpoints had just refused. || ROUND 1 ALSO raised one BELOW-GATE observation, correctly withheld from the findings: a comment this branch added at step-7-trade-card/page.tsx claimed 'every send path below refuses such a card', which is false -- `checkTradeRisk` runs only in SendToBrokerDialog, so a direct Place Limit / Right Now-Market on a stripped card stores `PortfolioPosition.stop = null`. Not a wrong number (the field is already nullable and both alert engines skip a null stop), so per the severity gate the BEHAVIOUR is logged against main, not fixed in-branch; only the false comment -- this branch's own text -- was corrected. || ROUND 2 (2026-09-09): CLEAN. ZERO gate-level findings, so per audit_rule v2 the phase is DONE -- a zero-finding round triggers no fixes, and the round that reviewed the last batch of fixes was already the second look. Scoped per the rule to round 1's FIX ONLY (2b770e9) plus its interactions, not the cumulative diff. What round 2 EXECUTED rather than reasoned about: drove the real get_watchlist over schema_version in {None,0,1,2,3} and confirmed None/0/1 fall through to the live fetch while 2/3 serve the scan -- the `is not None` -> `>=` polarity inversion is correct; confirmed the only value where `(x or 0)` differs from `is None` is a stored 0, which nothing writes and which the comparison correctly refuses; enumerated every `ScanResult(` construction in backend/app (exactly two, both stamped, both still enumerated by the AST test at test_scan_result_vintage.py:113); hunted for a FOURTH unguarded reader of the persisted blob and found none -- `scheduled_scan_runs.result_json` is read only by _compute_deltas, which touches `symbol` and `stockScore`, neither changed by piece 3, and the stock-scan path uses StockScanResult, which piece 3 never touched and which correctly does not share this constant; verified STALE_VERSIONS' sort key short-circuits on the bool so None never compares against an int; and re-ran the fail-then-pass proof BOTH ways -- all four app files reverted (6 fail) AND the three routers reverted while keeping VERSION=2, which is the faithful 'next bump forgotten' scenario (2 fail). || ROUND 2 raised ONE below-gate item, correctly excluded from the findings, and it was FIXED ANYWAY as a deliberate exception to the fix-only-gate-level rule -- stated here so the exception is on the record rather than silent. The two /api/watchlist tests round 1 added were TAUTOLOGICAL: they re-implemented the guard expression against a locally parsed blob instead of calling get_watchlist, and reverting watchlist.py to `is not None` left all 17 green. So round 1's own claim that the endpoint 'gained vintage tests it never had' was true only in that files existed -- the guard was still untested and the NEXT bump would have been caught for /scan/last and /api/tradecards but not here, which is precisely the root cause round 1 claimed to have closed. It is also the same defect this file's docstring records rounds 4 and 5 catching in the stamping test. Rationale for fixing rather than logging: the rule exists to stop fix-churn keeping the loop alive, and the loop had ALREADY terminated on a zero-finding round; this is a test-only change, in this branch's own new code, that makes a false claim true. Now drives the real endpoint through a two-select stub with the live-fetch path stubbed to nothing, so a scan-decided row (score 80 / PASS) is unmistakable against a fallback row (score 0 / NO_DATA) -- and reverting ONLY watchlist.py's guard now turns it red (verified). No round 3: the loop closed on round 2, and a test-only change verified to fail-then-pass is its own proof. || FINAL: backend 2156 passed / 1 skipped, frontend 111 suites / 1367 tests, typecheck clean, state.py no drift.

phases.name: Piece 4 -- per-position premium stop
phases.note: Built and green. TWO adversarial rounds run, NEITHER clean. Round 1 found 8 defects (all fixed). Round 2 found 8 more in this phase alone, all fixed: the frontend PREMIUM_STOP copied only one of the backend's two guards, so a failed quote (currentPrice coerced to 0) fired a Critical toast for EVERY position on every 30s cycle with no backend alert behind it -- a regression the pnlPct test it replaced did not have; the card displayed one premium stop and posted another, twice over (the reset re-seeds the field without telling the parent cache, and mergePlan swaps `exit` under an overridden card without changing `contract` so nothing re-runs -- the second reproduced the 78% stop that round 1 was supposed to have killed); a dollar stop at or beyond the entry fell back silently and also discarded a valid client-sent fraction; the drawer cleared the override on any entry >= 100 and persisted every keystroke, so typing '45' armed a 4% stop; the server-derived fraction was dropped from the create response, leaving the two engines disagreeing until the next sync; a dead schema field; and two tests that asserted plumbing while claiming to cover behaviour -- the router derivation and the PATCH write had NO test, and now go through the endpoint. NOT YET CLEAN -- round 3 pending. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. The CRITICAL was the same display-vs-posted split round 2 thought it had closed, reached by REVERSING the order of the two events: an unrelated edit BEFORE a mergePlan caches the old seed, the re-seed effect then moves the field without telling the parent, and premiumStopDollarToSend compared the stale cache against the NEW seed and let it through -- card showing $0.80 while $1.50 was posted. Root cause was inferring touched-ness by comparing values; it is now TRACKED and threaded to the page via onEditsChange's meta.touched.premiumStop, which also fixes the mirror defect (a user who typed the seed's own value back had the choice discarded). Also: the offline-retry path in syncFromBackend dropped the server-derived premiumStopPct, leaving the two engines disagreeing; the auto-trader test asserted the resolver directly and never called fire() or _check_daily_loss, so BOTH call sites could be reverted with 75 tests still green (replaced with two that drive the service and fail on that mutation); entryPrice had no gt=0 so a non-positive entry silently dropped the user's dollar stop unlogged; the drawer rewrote a stored stop on a bare focus-and-blur (0.4843 rendered '48' and committed 0.48) and could not represent sub-1% or >=99.5% fractions at all; and the persisted store gained two fields with no version bump (now v3). phases.name: Heston pricer -- Fourier inversion (Q8)
phases.note: F1 (THE PRICER) IS BUILT on claude/dev-state-reconstruction-hzmzbi at cf3da087 plus the round-1 audit fixes. Spec: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-heston-calibration-spec.md, and READ ITS SECTION 0a FIRST -- the build falsified two of the spec's own claims. || WHAT WAS WRONG: heston_price's _integrand re-applied exp(i*phi*lnS)/exp(i*phi*lnK) on top of a characteristic function that already carried e^{i*phi*ln(S/K)}. The moneyness exponents collected to 2i*phi*ln(S/K) + j*ln(S/K): a DOUBLED Fourier frequency plus a spurious (S/K)^j on P1, which also never divided by the Bakshi-Madan normaliser f2(-i)=S*e^{rT}. Error exactly zero at K==S (why it survived), +451% at 45 DTE and +2782% at 180 DTE in the |delta| 0.15-0.90 band scan.py ranks. _heston_char_fn was and is CORRECT and was NOT touched. || VERIFIED, not asserted: against an independently written reference (the two-CF form reaching P1 via b1=kappa-rho*sigma, u1=+1/2 rather than the Bakshi-Madan shift) the corrected pricer agrees to 0.000000% over 112 points, 7-365 DTE x 140-275 strikes. sigma_v->0 collapse to Black-Scholes: worst 0.0139% over 46 points, where the old code failed by 83161%. It is also 1.24-1.36x FASTER (test_heston_perf's realistic chain 0.56s -> 0.35s) because the correct integrand needs fewer quad subdivisions. || THE GATE-LEVEL NUMBER: on test_trade_plan's _plan() fixture (spot 318.73, K 375, 185 DTE, premium 7.47) the exit premium falls 12.52 -> 3.80 and the displayed R/R FLIPS +1.13 -> -0.82. The card was recommending, at +1.13, a trade whose first target leaves the position under water. || READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING ANY 'Heston repriced' NUMBER: F1 DOES NOT MAKE THE CARD RIGHT. It fixes the pricer; v0_grid=[0.04] is untouched until F2. Measured on the spec's reference chain with the shipped reduced grid through the POST-F1 pricer: rel-RMSE 0.645 at 45 DTE against a flat-BS baseline of 0.197 (3.27x WORSE than one flat volatility) and 0.754 vs 0.563 at 180 DTE (1.34x worse). Per strike, post-F1 Heston sits 27% to 100% BELOW the market mid across the whole band. scan.py still accepts method=='heston_grid' and labels it 'Heston repriced'. So the defect's DIRECTION flipped (wrong HIGH -> wrong LOW) and F1 is still a large net improvement, because the pricer error it removes dwarfs the calibration error it leaves -- but F2 IS NOT OPTIONAL POLISH, it is the other half of one defect, and its section 3.3 baseline gate is what makes shipping a fit seven times worse than a flat vol impossible. || SCOPE GREW BY ONE MEASURED DEFECT during the audit, and it is in F1's own stated scope (the two quad calls): the spec's 'the quadrature limits (500, limit=100) are measured sufficient' is FALSE. The integrands decay as exp(-0.5*v*T*phi^2), so the needed cutoff scales as 1/sqrt(v*T); a fixed 500 is 0.769% wrong at v0=0.01, theta=0.02, 1 DTE at the money. Reachable: v0=0.01 is in the grid under HESTON_FULL_CALIBRATION, heston_chain passes weeklies, and F2's chain seeding reaches it by default on a low-IV underlying. Now adaptive: min(max(500, sqrt(50/(v*T))), 20000) at v=min(v0,theta), limit=200. Worst error over 324 cases 0.769% -> 0.00218%, at 1.00x latency (the formula returns <500 for every expiry at the production default v0=theta=0.04). This also cut the worst out-of-band below-forward-intrinsic shortfall 0.127316 -> 0.002235; the two were one defect. || SIX existing tests pinned pricer output, NOT the four the spec's section 5.3 listed. Two lost their premise entirely (their fixtures no longer produce the 'artifact' dip, because the dip WAS this bug) and are renamed: test_estimate_targets_real_fixture_preserves_t3_after_t2_artifact -> ..._ladder_is_clean_and_all_heston, and test_trade_plan's test_heston_params_floors_non_monotonic_target_instead_of_falling_back -> test_heston_params_thread_through_to_a_clean_all_heston_ladder. Reverting the integrand now fails exactly those six and nothing else, so the set is closed. || THE LADDER FLOOR IN reward_risk.py IS DELIBERATELY RETAINED (spec section 4 scopes removal out; it only ever raises a level) but its comment no longer claims the dip is an inherent integration quirk, and it now states the cost of retention: the one mechanism it was built for is gone, so a dip reaching that branch most likely means the PRICER has regressed and the floor will quietly raise it instead of surfacing it. The two rewritten fixture tests assert STRICT increase for that reason. || TESTS: new backend/tests/test_heston_price.py, 7 invariants / 19 pytest cases. A four-mutation battery fails 4 / 13 / 13 / 1 cases (rho flipped; K* dropped from P1; the S*e^{rT} normaliser dropped; the cutoff reverted to 500). THE rho FLIP IS WHY THE SKEWED-PARAMETER TESTS EXIST: the spec's section 5.1 as written pinned the pricer only where it degenerates to Black-Scholes, so inverting rho -- destroying the entire skew -- passed every test in it. Two of the 19 cases (put-call parity, no-arbitrage bounds) do NOT catch this bug and say so in their own docstrings: the put is derived from the call by parity, and the pre-F1 errors all landed inside [forward intrinsic, cap]. || Backend suite 2240 passed / 1 skipped (2221 baseline + 19 new). Backend-only change; no frontend file is touched, so the frontend typecheck cannot move. || ROUND 2 (2026-09-13) CAME BACK CLEAN -- ZERO gate-level findings, so audit_clean is true and F1 is DONE per audit_rule v2 clause 3 (one zero-finding round ends it). SCOPED TO 188e2526 ALONE -- the round-1 FIX commit -- per the shrinking-target clause, exactly as Phase E's round 2 was; cf3da087 and the spec commit were NOT re-audited as targets. || WHAT ROUND 2 PROBED, recorded so the absence of findings is auditable rather than merely asserted: (1) reward_risk.py proved behaviour-neutral by AST equality against cf3da087 -- text differs, ast.dump identical -- so the round-1 edit there really is comment-only; (2) all 12 _REFERENCE_PRICES and the 3 short-expiry/low-variance values re-derived against an INDEPENDENTLY WRITTEN two-CF Heston (Heston 1993 + Albrecher little-trap branch, u1=+1/2, b1=kappa-rho*sigma_v), matching to <=1.9e-11 relative; (3) the adaptive cutoff swept over 29760 cases -- the full env-gated grid plus the bs_fallback shapes x 10 expiries from 0.25 to 547 DTE x 6 moneyness x call/put -- worst ABSOLUTE error $0.000695, worst relative 0.3828% on a $0.110 option, and ZERO scipy IntegrationWarnings, which also establishes that the `except Exception -> bs_price` silent-substitution path is never reached over that space; (4) the phi==0.0 unreachability claim instrumented over 16.5M characteristic-function evaluations -- 0 hits, smallest phi seen 2.86e-3 -- so moving the quad lower limit from 1e-10 to 0 is safe; (5) a mutation battery on the changed lines in which revert-to-500, 50->5, the full quad-arg revert, dropping the max(500,...) floor and lower=1.0 were all KILLED, while min->max in v_eff, cap 20000->800 and limit=200->20 SURVIVED the suite but were then measured to move no production price by more than 0.8 of a cent and only under HESTON_FULL_CALIBRATION, which is set nowhere in the repo -- so no test-coverage gap clears the bar round 1's rho finding cleared; (6) calibration latency old vs new, 1 DTE 0.265s -> 0.337s against _CALIBRATION_TIMEOUT=1.0, so the wider cutoff cannot silently degrade a card from 'Heston repriced' to the BS fallback. || TWO COMMENT CLAIMS IN heston.py ARE FALSE. Both re-verified in this session, both LOGGED AGAINST MAIN and deliberately NOT fixed in-branch per audit_rule's fixing clause -- a comment is below the gate: it puts no wrong number in front of a user and corrupts no persisted data. See the two open_questions entries dated 2026-09-13.

phases.name: Heston calibration -- seed, objective, baseline gate (Q8)
phases.note: BUILT 2026-09-13, ZERO ADVERSARIAL ROUNDS. On claude/heston-calibration-f2 at 6950b098. || HOW IT GOT HERE, because the provenance matters: the code was found UNCOMMITTED in an ephemeral container by a session that did not write it -- a stop hook caught it. It was committed unchanged rather than lost, and the commit message says so. It has NOT been reviewed line by line by anyone. || WHAT IS BUILT, read off the diff and confirmed by grep: all three spec-section-3 parts. (1) `_seed_v0` solves v0 out of the chain -- the mean implied vol over the strikes that invert, via the BRACKETED _compute_iv_bs, with the days-vs-expiry_years unit trap handled at the call site (expiry_years * 365.0). (2) `_rel_rmse` replaces the absolute-dollar objective. (3) `_flat_bs_baseline` plus the gate returning method='bs_flat'; scan.py still tests `== 'heston_grid'`, so bs_flat is discarded with no call-site change, exactly as the spec predicted. Ties go to the baseline. Both logging decisions are implemented: `_boundary_hits` and the ladder floor both log at WARNING, and the file argues WARNING rather than INFO from uvicorn's default logging config leaving the root logger handler-less at WARNING. || ALL FOUR SPEC 5.2 TESTS EXIST among 20 in backend/tests/test_heston_calibration.py (522 lines), plus additions to test_reward_risk.py. || MEASURED THIS SESSION ON THE SPEC's OWN REFERENCE CHAIN (section 7's recipe: S=201.86, r=0.05, ATM/SKEW/CURV = 0.345/0.45/1.6, strikes every $5, in band |bs_delta| in [0.15, 0.90]) -- THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS FIXED: at 45 DTE the gate now ACCEPTS at rel-RMSE 0.0796 against a flat-BS baseline of 0.1969, beating one flat volatility by 2.5x. Pre-F2 the same chain measured 0.645 vs 0.197, i.e. 3.27x WORSE. The v0 seed lands at 0.1245 (35.28% vol) where the old grid offered 0.04 (20%). At 180 DTE it also beats the baseline (0.3163 vs 0.3965) when it is allowed to finish. || BUT LONG-DATED CHAINS SIT ON THE TIMEOUT, and this is the one thing an audit must look at first. MEASURED: the 28-strike 180-DTE reference chain takes 1.02s against `_CALIBRATION_TIMEOUT = 1.0`, so whether a fit that BEATS the baseline reaches a card is decided by machine load rather than by fit quality; the 10-strike 45-DTE chain is comfortable at 0.30s. When the budget is missed, calibrate_cached returns bs_fallback -- AND THE INNER CALL HAS ALREADY LOGGED 'accepted (heston_grid)'. That directly contradicts the file's own stated principle ('Decide the verdict BEFORE logging it. The log line names the label this call actually returns'), which holds on every path except this one. NO WRONG NUMBER REACHES A CARD -- a correct fit is silently WITHHELD, not a wrong one shown -- so it is below the gate by the letter of audit_rule, but it defeats the diagnostic F2 itself added. || THIS REOPENS A DECISION TAKEN ONE DAY EARLIER: F2-OUT-OF-SCOPE-THREE-2026-09-13 filed `_CALIBRATION_TIMEOUT does not bound latency` as exactitude, on the reasoning that F1 made the grid cheaper so the pressure went DOWN. That reasoning was sound for F1 and is wrong for F2: F2 adds the baseline sweep to the same budget, and the file's own comment records a first cut at 280 evals that pushed the 180-DTE chain from 0.547s to 1.156s 'and straight through _CALIBRATION_TIMEOUT'. It was optimised to 46 evals for exactly this reason and still lands at 1.02s. || AUDITED 2026-09-13: CLEAN AFTER 2 ROUNDS, zero gate-level findings in each. Round 1 ran 14 mutations (13 caught) and reproduced every number the diff's own comments assert. ROUND 2 WAS RUN ANYWAY, deliberately, and the reasoning is worth keeping: audit_rule v2 says one zero-finding round ends the loop, but its stated justification is 'the round that reviewed the last batch of fixes was already the second look' -- and F2 had no such round. A first-pass clean on code nobody had reviewed line by line is the one case that exit clause does not model. Round 2 was briefed to FALSIFY round 1's claims rather than repeat its work; it confirmed most, corrected three, and found nine new below-gate items. || A CORRECTION TO THIS NOTE'S OWN EARLIER TEXT, made by round 2: the pre-audit version of this note reported the accepted fit's worst selectable-band error as '6.7% at 30 DTE rising to 28.1% at 180 DTE'. Those two figures are exact -- round 2 reproduced them to the decimal -- but they are ONE CHAIN's numbers, not a bound, and the phrasing invited reading ~28% as a ceiling. Holding everything else fixed and steepening the smile to skew 0.80 / curv 3.0, still a plausible equity surface, the accepted fit's worst in-band error is 31.5% at 30 DTE and 77.5% at 180 DTE -- and it still passes the gate. Across a wider shape sweep accepted fits reached 61.9% (30 DTE) and 99.6% (365 DTE). ~28% is nearer the FLOOR of the long-dated range than its ceiling. This does not change the verdict on the commit: F2 reduced the error in EVERY case measured (pre-F2 the same chains were 75.0% -> 6.7%, 82.3% -> 28.1%, 86.6% -> 31.5%, 93.8% -> 77.5%). But the gate is purely RELATIVE to a flat vol and has no absolute acceptance threshold, so it cannot bound what reaches a card. || VERIFIED, and ONLY this: full backend suite 2262 passed / 1 skipped, exit 0, which RECONCILES -- main stood at 2240 / 1 after F1 and this adds exactly its 22 new cases. Frontend NOT run and deliberately so: the diff touches zero files under frontend/. GREEN IS NOT CLEAN.

Measured on step 5's .stepBody (overflow-x: auto): scrollWidth 1350 at rest, 1408 while the GATE badge is hovered -- the same 58px, back. already_shipped.note: Revives scripts/state.py's audit-bookkeeping probe, which had returned None on EVERY run since 2026-09-09 and rendered "No drift" throughout. Tests in backend/tests/test_state_audit_bookkeeping.py drive a real temporary git repo rather than mocking subprocess, because both defects were about which value reached git; all three defect-restoring mutants are killed. || ROUND 1 (2026-09-16) RETURNED FOUR GATE-LEVEL FINDINGS, all fixed in-branch. (1) With neither origin/main nor main resolving -- a --single-branch or --depth 1 clone -- the probe returned None, which renders as "No drift": a clean bill for a check that never ran, the very observable this change exists to remove. (2) THE SHARPEST: the round number was taken over the WHOLE branch while the pointer resolves ONE piece, so a branch carrying two pieces answered for the earlier piece's rounds -- a red banner on an entirely honest file whose printed remedy ("record the count there") could only be satisfied by writing a number known to be false into this file. _pointer_scoped_base now walks the state file's own history and stops where active_phase last differed. The commit that MOVES the pointer therefore stayed inside the new pointer's range -- and recording the round that just finished while moving the pointer is ONE commit in this repo's actual style ("Record round 4: clean at the gate...", "Phase G is in: name the merge, clear the active phase", "The bearish gate is in: name the merge, clear the branch"). A piece with zero rounds of its own drew red DRIFT for the previous piece's round number, clearable only by merging or by writing a false count. The walk now takes the OLDEST commit still carrying the pointer -- the one that set it -- and excludes it. Round 2 also proved the round-1 test pinned the defect rather than the behaviour, which is why that assertion was rewritten rather than kept. Four of round 2's below-gate items were inside the function being rewritten and were fixed with it: the (ref, detail) contract was only true on failure, the unborn-HEAD diagnosis blamed a clone flag, json.loads caught only ValueError so a non-object state file would traceback the SessionStart hook, and exhausting _POINTER_SCAN_LIMIT degraded to the FULL range -- back to the pre-fix false positive rather than to something safe. || ROUND 3 (2026-09-16) RETURNED ONE GATE-LEVEL FINDING, again inside the PREVIOUS ROUND'S FIX -- the third round running without going clean, which is audit_rule's HARD CAP: STOP AUDITING AND TELL KENNETH. When active_phase TRANSITIONS to null inside the range, round 2's boundary change (take the OLDEST commit still carrying the pointer and EXCLUDE it) collapses the range to empty -- the clearing commit is the newest state-file commit, so it becomes the boundary and is excluded, leaving `git log HEAD..HEAD`. The third option -- ask whether ANY already_shipped entry accounts for the rounds -- is the comparison audit_bookkeeping_drift's own docstring rejects as useless, because Phase D's 13 rounds are a global maximum nothing can exceed. || REACHABILITY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: this repo has never cleared the pointer on a branch. already_shipped.note: KENNETH'S CALL 2026-09-16, taken over patching the two open doors one at a time, on the evidence that three consecutive fixes had each contained the next instance of the same shape. || ROUND 1 RAN AND WAS NOT CLEAN: FIVE gate-level findings, and one of them was a REGRESSION SHIPPED AT d5fcbce -- the new code rendered "No drift" at exit 0 on undercounts the code it replaced had caught. Reproduced independently before it was accepted: five rounds in the subjects, the file declaring anything from 1 to 4, SILENT; only declared==0 still fired. THE REASONING IN THE DOCSTRING WAS INVERTED. It claimed recording a count could not move the boundary forward because the boundary is defined by counts BELOW the declared one -- but raising `declared` makes MORE historical commits qualify as lower, and the NEWEST qualifying one wins, so raising the count moved the boundary FORWARD. In this repo's style, where every branch commit touches this file, the newest state-file commit almost always declares less than the live one, so it became the boundary and the window collapsed. A working-tree-only bump did it too, which is option A's finding 1 resurrected through the count field. FIXED HERE: the count supplies no boundary at all. The boundary is the commit that INTRODUCED the entry, which is where the entry APPEARED rather than what it SAYS, so recording a number -- true or false, committed or not -- cannot move it. || THE ACCEPTED COST IS NOW STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED, and pinned by a test: an entry that predates the branch point is never ABSENT in range, gets no narrowing, and answers for the whole branch including an earlier piece's rounds, on an honest file. A false ALARM, visible, clearing by merging or by recording the count -- the deliberate trade against ever going silent on an undercount. || THE CAP WAS ALSO FIXED, and it was a real defect of the same family: gating on the self-reported `audit_rounds` made the banner UNCLEARABLE once a piece passed three unclean rounds on work that could not yet merge -- going clean is only honest when it IS clean, lowering the count trips the undercount check, re-pointing moves the complaint. Round 4 finding 6's rule broken by the block that cites it. It now counts what THIS BRANCH still carries (`git_max`), so merging empties it exactly as for the unphased banner, a stale pointer at finished work no longer fires, and resuming already-escalated merged work no longer re-fires. || AND THE VERIFY PROBE WAS ROUND 1 FINDING 4'S MODELLING ERROR AGAIN, committed inside the test written to prevent it: it anchored on `_declared_rounds_at(...)` and on the cap's CONDITION, and the test 'proved' it tracked behaviour by mutating exactly those two strings. Every real behavioural revert left both anchors standing. A NEGATIVE full_conviction_pct is deliberately NOT treated that way -- it has no documented meaning, and guessing one would size a live order off a number nobody chose, so it refuses. ALSO CAUGHT WHILE BUILDING, and each is a fail-open that reached the broker: a bool (min_mult: true is 1.0 to float(), i.e. full size from a value that is not a multiplier) and nan/inf, which survive every max()/min() range check and reach round() in fire() as a nan quantity. [SUPERSEDED BY ROUND 2, see below: the bound is (1, 100] -- EXCLUSIVE at 1, which is the whole of R2-G1.] A value like 4 (a dropped zero from 40) is still in range and still honourable -- no bound can separate it from a deliberate 4, and inventing a floor is the thing I refused to do for negatives. decisions.a: DECISION, LOCKED by Kenneth 2026-09-20: MOVE SIZING ONTO THE PER-SYMBOL MEASUREMENT, AND LAND PIECE B FIRST. Both halves accepted, the ordering explicitly included. || THE LEADING ARGUMENT IS THAT THIS IS NOT A NEW POLICY. It is OPTIONS ONLY -- auto_trader.py calls `execute_option_order` and nothing else, and there is no stock auto-trade path (StockAutoTradeArm is a strategy-WATCH subscription, not /auto-trade/arm). The STOCK path has sized off the symbol's own direction-framed conviction since it was built (stock_scan.py:973-979, at scan time, scaling the risk budget into `shares`). So this puts options on the input stocks already use; options are the outlier. || THE OTHER FOUR REASONS: it removes an inconsistency 072d74ff itself introduced (before it, gate and sizer at least agreed -- both SPX); it is nearly free mechanically because `_measure_trade_regime` already runs on every gated fire and sizing currently throws the result away; it DELETES `get_last_conviction` from the fire path along with the unbounded cache staleness round 1 flagged, closing a deferred item rather than adding one; and the risk is two-sided rather than a size-up, so it does not inherit piece 3's 'moves slowest' posture. || WHY PIECE B FIRST, AND THIS IS THE PART KENNETH WAS ASKED TO ACCEPT EXPLICITLY: today a malformed `direction` on a direct constructor falls to the `else` branch and sizes off a wrongly-mirrored number -- wrong, but BOUNDED between min_mult and 1. After the swap it would make compute_omm raise, `_measure_trade_regime` abstain, and -- if sizing treats 'unmeasurable' the way the GATE does -- the order would leave at the FULL ARMED QUANTITY. Unbounded, on the most malformed input. The swap RELOCATES piece B's hole and makes it worse, so piece B's guard lands first. || MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, computed with the real conviction_mult on the live config (min_mult 0.3, full_conviction_pct 40) for the audit's own reproduced case -- MSFT Position, 4 contracts armed, measured production SPX +27: BEARISH -27 -> +50, mult 0.414 -> 1.000, qty 2 -> 4 (DOUBLES). BULLISH +27 -> -50, mult 0.886 -> 0.300, qty 4 -> 1 (4x CUT). Directionally correct, since MSFT's own regime was bearish -- but not small, and Kenneth saw these numbers before agreeing. || SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT, NOT A PREFERENCE: in a bull market bearish trades are currently FLOORED by a market-wide bullish number, so this swap systematically RAISES BEARISH SIZE. Piece 3's two-sided ramp (already on this branch at 3371d023, ZERO rounds) also raises the opposed half (neutral 0.30 -> 0.65). THE TWO COMPOUND AND BOTH ARE UNAUDITED, so this must land and go CLEAN BEFORE piece 3's round opens, never alongside it. || TWO THINGS THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST ANSWER DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN DISCOVER: (1) what sizing does when the regime is UNMEASURABLE -- the gate abstains and fires, and sizing must NOT copy that, because abstain-to-full-size is the largest position on the worst input. (2) With `regime_gate.enabled: false` nothing measures today, and `test_regime_gate_does_not_fire_when_disabled` asserts `fetch_spy.call_count == 0`. Sizing-on-per-symbol needs the measurement on that path too, so that test gets UPDATED WITH A REASON, never deleted.

decisions.q: Round 3 of STATE-PROBE-REVIVAL found that scripts/state.py's audit-bookkeeping probe goes SILENT when active_phase is null and the branch carries uncounted rounds -- full detail in the already_shipped entry of that name. _pointer_scoped_base narrows the range for EVERY pointer value including null, so a commit that peels the pointer off BECOMES the excluded boundary and the window collapses to empty. A branch that runs four rounds and then records the piece UNDERCOUNTED while clearing the pointer in one commit renders "No drift" at exit 0. Clearing the pointer became an escape hatch from the undercount check. Three options were put to Kenneth. (A) Do not narrow when the pointer is null, so the unphased banner fires again. (B) Change no code and write down the convention that the pointer is cleared in the merge commit, never earlier. (C) Teach the unphased path to read already_shipped counts so it can tell an honest cleared pointer from a dishonest one.
decisions.a: KENNETH CHOSE (A) on 2026-09-16, AND IT IS NOW BUILT -- see the already_shipped entry 'STATE-PROBE-NULL-POINTER -- a cleared pointer is not a scope' for what shipped and how it was mutation-verified. It is built but NOT YET AUDITED. WHAT WAS BUILT, as specified: in _pointer_scoped_base, return `base_ref` unnarrowed when the pointer is falsy (`if not active: return base_ref`, before the `git log`), PLUS the test that does not exist today -- build a branch that opens a piece, runs rounds 1-4, then records it undercounted while clearing the pointer in ONE commit, and assert the probe reports drift. NO test currently exercises _pointer_scoped_base with a null pointer, which is exactly how the regression got through round 2. || WHY (A), so it is not re-litigated: a false ALL-CLEAR is silent and nobody ever finds it, while a false ALARM is visible and self-correcting -- and this entire piece exists because a false all-clear ran for a week while four rounds shipped unseen. (A)'s cost is a banner on an HONEST file in the one workflow where the pointer is cleared BEFORE the merge, and that banner clears by merging or by re-pointing, both of which are honest actions; it is NOT the round-1 shape whose only escape was writing a number known to be false. Measured, not assumed: across the last 25 state-file commits this repo has never cleared the pointer on a branch -- every value->null transition is the merge-naming commit on main -- so in practice the banner would essentially never be seen. (B) was rejected because a probe that works only while nobody deviates from a habit is the shape of the bug this piece was built to remove. (C) was rejected because audit_bookkeeping_drift's own docstring shows the comparison can never fire: Phase D's 13 clean rounds are a global maximum nothing can exceed. || THE HARD CAP IS NOT BEING WORKED AROUND. Three rounds ran on STATE-PROBE-REVIVAL and none came back clean, so there is NO fourth round on that piece. audit_rule's own remedy for a batch too big to audit is to SPLIT IT, so this one-line fix plus its test is a NEW and deliberately tiny batch that gets ONE fresh adversarial round of its own. If that round does not come back clean, STOP AND TELL KENNETH rather than starting another.

decisions.q: Step 2's audit found (G2-5) that moving the four card-edit caches off the step-7 page and into a persisted store silently removed the thing that used to clear them -- the page UNMOUNT. The stamp replaces it for a NEW SCAN but not for the passage of TIME, so a typed entry limit survived indefinitely under one scan_id: don't re-scan, reload tomorrow, and the button still promises $2.71 against a mid that has moved. Three options were put to Kenneth: (a) leave it -- the numbers are the user's own and the stamp covers the case that INVENTS numbers; (b) age the slice and drop edits older than N hours; (c) persist only `picks`, which is what Q3 actually asked to survive a reload, and let the typed prices die on a reload again.
