There is no scheduler or scan-driven arm path. SO THE SELL BRANCH IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE UI, and changing `100 - conviction` to `-conviction` WOULD CHANGE NO LIVE TRADE WHILE APPEARING TO CLOSE THE BUG. That is the worst available outcome: a closed item, a green suite, and the money defect still live. || THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE OTHER BRANCH. Every bearish trade takes `directional_conv = conviction` -- the BULLISH frame -- so the ramp is EXACTLY INVERTED for bearish trades: largest into the regime that opposes the trade, smallest into the one that favours it. || CORRECTED NUMBERS, COMPUTED against conviction_mult on the shipped block (min_mult 0.3, full 40). For a bearish long put at bullish conviction C, correct is mult(-C), actual is mult(C): C=+40 -> should 0.30, gets 1.00 (3.33x OVERSIZED into a strongly bullish regime); C=+20 -> should 0.30, gets 0.65; C=0 -> should 0.30, gets 0.30, NO ERROR AT ALL; C=-40 -> should 1.00, gets 0.30 (3.33x UNDERSIZED into the regime that favours the trade). THE NEUTRAL ROW IS WHERE BOTH THE ORIGINAL ENTRY AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE PLAN WENT WRONG: conviction_mult clamps `frac = max(0.0, min(conv/full, 1.0))`, a ONE-SIDED ramp, so neutral is the FLOOR and not the mid-ramp. The error is zero at neutral and grows symmetrically outward. || BLAST RADIUS IS QUANTITY-DEPENDENT and the original entry's '10 -> 3' framing overstates it: `adjusted_qty = max(1, round(quantity * mult))`, so AT AN ARMED QUANTITY OF 1 -- the common single-leg arm -- THE DEFECT HAS NO EFFECT WHATSOEVER (1 either way). It bites from qty 2 up, and the 3.33x figure is multiplier-space, realised at qty 10. Still gate-level: it reaches live broker order sizes. || THE ORIGINAL'S MEASURED CLAIMS ('at conviction 0 a SELL goes out at 10 where the correct mirror gives 3', '+20 goes out at 10 versus 3', 'only the deep-bearish end happens to come out right') are all arithmetic about the UNREACHABLE branch and should not be read as measurements of live behaviour. || THE TEST CLAIM SURVIVES, WITH A DIFFERENT NUMBER: test_auto_trader.py:514 does pin wrong behaviour, but the correction is not 'expect the floor on a SELL'. It is rewritten as the coherent case it was reaching for -- a bearish LONG PUT (action="BUY", direction="Bearish") -- and on its existing qty 4 / conviction 80 fixture the expected quantity is 1. || THE FIX IS NOT THE ONE-LINE MIRROR. Direction must be threaded explicitly from the card (ArmRequest and ArmedStrategy both gain a required `direction: Literal["Bullish", "Bearish"]`), because inferring direction from `action` is what caused this bug and inferring it from option_symbol's C/P depends on a field whose format is a tracked follow-up. PLAN: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-auto-trader-direction-sizing-plan.md -- adversarial round 1 returned 14 findings, all accepted; NOT YET CLEAN, NOT IMPLEMENTED. Two of round 1's findings are worth carrying here because they outlive the plan: a required field with no default 422s every arm body that omits it (at least 9 tests across test_auto_trade.py -- a DIFFERENT FILE from test_auto_trader.py -- plus test_phase_g_arm_pick.py's _arm_body helper and three direct ArmRequest constructions), and any test of this fix must arm quantity=4, because at quantity=1 the multipliers 0.30/0.65/1.00 all round to 1 and a full suite of them passes with the bug still in place. || ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW IS UNEDITED, including the two claims corrected above. || *** ANSWERED BY KENNETH 2026-09-17: TAKE IT AS ITS OWN PIECE WITH A FULL ROUND -- plan, adversarial rounds until the plan is clean, implement, then adversarial rounds on the code until that is clean too. The defect is ONE LINE, in the fire path only -- auto_trader.py:176 -- because regime_monitor.py:184 is the only producer that pins direction='Bullish' and caches the bullish frame. AND ONE TEST PINS THE WRONG BEHAVIOUR: test_auto_trader.py:513 test_vol_sizing_sell_reduced_in_strongly_bullish_market asserts 'SELL at conviction=80 -> bearish_conv=20 ... must reduce 4 to 3'. The correct mirror gives -80, clamped to 0, so the floor: 4 -> min_mult. Same shape as Q1 -- a test to be CORRECTED, not deleted, and its comment explains the wrong arithmetic. || ORIGINAL STOP-AND-TELL, unedited: STOP-AND-TELL, 2026-09-17, AND IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS THE BEARISH GATE YOU JUST MERGED. Found by SIZING-FAIL-CLOSED's round 3, correctly EXCLUDED from that round's clean verdict because it is outside the diff, and INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED before being written here. But conviction_pct is a SIGNED scale: regime_omm.conviction() returns `signal if direction == 'Bullish' else -signal` over P(Bull) - P(Bear), so it runs -100..+100, conviction_label calls -15..+15 Neutral and formats it {:+d}%, and regime_monitor fills the cache with direction='Bullish' and documents it as the 'bullish frame'. The mirror of a signed conviction is -conviction, NOT 100 - conviction. MEASURED on the shipped block (min_mult 0.3, full 40) with an armed quantity of 10: at conviction 0 (neutral) a SELL goes out at 10 where the correct mirror gives 3; at +20 it goes out at 10 versus 3; at +40 -- a STRONGLY BULLISH regime -- it still goes out at 10 versus 3. The bullish side is correct throughout. SAME SHAPE AS 49ffa53: a bearish-side transform written as though the scale were unsigned 0-100 while the code that produces it is direction-aware. It sizes live broker orders, so it is gate-level on main. MEASURED, before and after: the 28-strike 180-DTE reference chain's inner calibration is 0.834s pre-F2 and 1.03-1.06s post-F2, so a chain that used to return heston_grid now returns bs_fallback -- F2 WITHHOLDS a fit that BEATS the baseline (0.3163 vs 0.3965). Worse, it is not confined to long-dated chains: under concurrency a 45-DTE / 10-strike chain that takes 0.325s solo returned bs_fallback on ALL 8 of 8 concurrent calls, and the scanner runs symbols concurrently. And `shutdown(wait=True)` means the 1s never bounded wall time anyway -- a 55-strike chain measures 2.25s inner / 2.38s wall. THREE SECOND-ORDER EFFECTS: (1) when the budget is missed the outer call returns bs_fallback WHILE THE INNER CALL HAS ALREADY LOGGED 'accepted (heston_grid)', contradicting the file's own principle that the log names the label actually returned -- true on every other path; (2) the timed-out inner call still populates the lru_cache, so the NEXT scan of the same chain returns heston_grid in 1ms, meaning two consecutive scans of one symbol can show different pricing models and different R/R; (3) lru_cache does not de-duplicate in-flight calls -- 8 concurrent identical calls produced misses=8, currsize=1, i.e. eight full grid searches for one entry. Each outcome is HONESTLY LABELLED, so no wrong number reaches a card and it stays below the gate -- but it means F2's measured improvement may reach production rarely or never. THIS SUPERSEDES the reasoning in F2-OUT-OF-SCOPE-THREE-2026-09-13, which filed the timeout as exactitude because 'F1 made the grid CHEAPER so the pressure went down'. True for F1. False for F2, which adds the baseline sweep to the same budget.  ---- HALF ANSWERED 2026-09-13 by TIMEOUT-DELETE-INNER-2026-09-13: the timeout is DELETED, so a completed fit is no longer discarded and the three second-order effects that flowed from it (a log naming a label the caller does not get, a timed-out call still populating the lru_cache so two consecutive scans show different models, an lru_cache that does not de-duplicate in flight) no longer have the inner timeout as a trigger -- the cache effects remain, on their own terms, since the cache is unchanged. THE HEADLINE CLAIM OF THIS ENTRY IS NOT ANSWERED: F2's win still reaches NO card, because 40 of 40 symbols are abandoned at the OUTER 2.0s guard. That is the GIL entry above, which now owns this question.

BELOW THE GATE, found by F1 round 1 and deliberately NOT fixed (spec section 4 scopes heston_price's put-call parity tail as unchanged, and no contract it affects can reach a card): heston_price clamps with max(price, 0.0) rather than at the true no-arbitrage floor, so quadrature truncation can leave a price slightly BELOW forward intrinsic. Measured across the full 243-combination grid x 7 expiries x moneyness 0.005x-9.9x: worst shortfall 0.002235 on a $1789.94 deep-ITM put (1.2e-6 relative), and EVERY violating point has |delta| == 1.0, which contract_rules.yaml rejects long before pricing. In band the count is zero across 43659 contracts. The high-accuracy reference returns exactly forward intrinsic at those points, so this is truncation, not a formula error. (It was 0.127316 before F1's adaptive cutoff landed, at v0=0.01/theta=0.02/1 DTE -- the same defect.) Tightening the clamp to max(price, forward_intrinsic) is two lines and provably never wrong, since a European option is worth at least its forward intrinsic by arbitrage. Worth doing the next time anyone is in heston.py; not worth its own change.

LATENT TRAP, pre-existing and NOT introduced by F1, logged rather than fixed (the spec scopes the except -> bs_price fallback as unchanged): heston_price wraps its quad calls in `except Exception`, and Warning subclasses Exception -- so in any process that escalates warnings to errors (pytest -W error, python -W error, a library calling simplefilter('error')), scipy's IntegrationWarning makes heston_price silently return bs_price(S, K, T, r, sqrt(v0), is_call) while every downstream label still says 'Heston repriced'. Demonstrated at v0=0.01, kappa=0.5, theta=0.02, sigma_v=0.6, rho=-0.8, K=1.0, 30 DTE: 200.85748282713888 normally, 200.86410115623582 under simplefilter('error'), the latter bit-identical to bs_price. Also: those IntegrationWarnings go to stderr from production code unsuppressed -- they fire at extreme moneyness (0.005x, 0.05x, 9.9x), all out of band. The honest fix is to catch the specific exceptions quad actually raises and to return a method/flag the caller can see, not to widen the except. No wrong number reaches a card today because nothing in this app escalates warnings.

RAISED BY F1 AND UNANSWERED -- the ladder floor in reward_risk.py now has no known mechanism to catch, and that makes it a MASK rather than a guard. It was written for a dip believed to be an inherent quirk of heston_price's integration; F1 proved the dip was the Fourier-inversion defect, and no fixture in the suite produces a natural dip any more. The floor is retained per spec section 4 (it only ever raises a level, and 'no dip on these fixtures' is not 'no dip on every live chain') and its comment now states this cost explicitly -- but a dip that DOES reach that branch most likely means the pricer has regressed, and the floor will quietly raise it instead of surfacing it. The two rewritten fixture tests assert STRICT increase as a partial mitigation, but they cover one fixture each, not the live path. Spec section 6.3 says remove it only after F1 has run against live chains long enough to say the artifact never appears. CONSIDER INSTEAD: make the floor LOG when it fires, so the live evidence accumulates by itself rather than waiting on someone to go looking for it.

THE DIRECTION-CONVICTION GATE CANNOT TELL 'MEASURED MEDIOCRE' FROM 'UNMEASURED', raised by the 2026-09-16 round-1 adversarial audit of the bearish-gate fix and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED in that change (it is a scorer-contract change, not a gate fix, and the gate fix was already touching both scan paths). The gate reads ONE integer, the trend rule's score, so the three ways stock_scorer.py says 'no measurement' are indistinguishable from a real score: _trend_relative_strength's missing-benchmark fallback returns CAUTION 50 (stock_scorer.py:332-340, with a logger.warning), _trend_additive/_trend_crossover return 0 for insufficient_data (:192, :263), and _rule_score / next(..., 50) default to 50 when no trend rule is present at all. CONSEQUENCES, all now SYMMETRIC across Bullish and Bearish where before the fix the bearish ceiling hid them: (a) score 50 clears every floor (30 Swing / 40 Position), so if trend_method is set to relative_strength via the Step-3 `trend_method` override (stock_scorer.py:1028) AND the SPY benchmark fetch fails -- which stock_scan.py:1122-1128 tolerates by design with an empty benchmark_closes -- EVERY symbol scores exactly 50 and the gate becomes a silent no-op for that scan; (b) score 0 for insufficient_data is rejected with reason 'direction_conviction: trend 0 < N', which classify_stock_rejection buckets as failed_direction, so ScanFunnel renders a DATA OUTAGE as 'Direction conviction - N no conviction' (frontend ScanFunnel/index.tsx:191) and tells the user the market has no bearish structure when it actually has no data. NOT REACHABLE via the missing-rule path: score_stock always emits a trend rule (stock_scorer.py:1089), so that default is defensive only -- the dead `if _c.stockBreakdown else 50` branch it fed in scan.py WAS removed. THE FIX IS A SCORER-CONTRACT CHANGE: RuleResult needs to carry whether the score was measured, and both gates need to refuse to count an unmeasured trend as conviction, with its own rejection reason so the funnel stops calling a data outage a market verdict. Kenneth's call on whether that is worth doing before the bearish engine is trusted with real puts.

THE DIRECTION-CONVICTION GATE IS STILL INVISIBLE TO THE USER, raised by the same 2026-09-16 audit and NOT fixed with the bearish-gate change (both halves are feature surface, not a correctness fix). (a) /stock-analysis builds gate_flags for price, score, regime_headwind, signal, backtest and confidence (stock_scan.py:356-521) but NOT for direction_conviction, although docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-29-single-stock-analysis-design.md:38,:48 names it in the gate list -- so a Bearish/Position name with trend 20 shows all-green on /analysis while the scanner rejects it for no conviction, and neither screen says why. (b) Every sibling threshold family has a config endpoint and a fetch-with-fallback store -- eventThresholdsStore, ivThresholdsStore, stopPremiumThresholdsStore -- and direction_conviction has neither, so the only user-visible artefact is 'N no conviction' in the funnel with no number attached. THAT IS THE POINT: this gate screened every non-Intraday scan BACKWARDS on the bearish side from 2026-06-18 to 2026-09-16 and nothing on screen showed the threshold it was applying.

ORIGINAL ENTRY FOLLOWS ---- LOGGED AGAINST MAIN by F2 round 2, NOT fixed in-branch (no wrong number -- but it defeats a decision taken one day earlier): THE GRID-BOUNDARY LOG IS TAUTOLOGICAL ON THE GRID THAT SHIPS. Decision F2-GRID-AND-EDGE-OF-BOX-2026-09-13 added `_boundary_hits` so that 'three of five pinned on one synthetic chain' would become evidence accumulating from Kenneth's real scans. It cannot: the production grid has exactly TWO rungs per searched dimension (kappa [0.5, 3.0], theta [0.02, 0.08], sigma_v [0.2, 0.6], rho [-0.8, -0.2]), so every possible winner is at a min or a max BY CONSTRUCTION -- enumerated, 16 of 16 reachable winners report all four pinned.
